# TACO: A Benchmark for Open-Domain Text-to-SQL with Ambiguous and Cross-Database Queries

[All reading notes](../reading-notes.md) · [Catalog entry](../README.md#taco)

**Full paper read · 2026-11-09**

[Original source](https://www.vldb.org/pvldb/vol19/p1386-fan.pdf) · PVLDB 19(6), 2026, pages 1386-1399

**Reading coverage:** All fourteen PDF pages, Sections 1-6, synthesis and expert annotation procedures, equations, Tables 1-6 and Figures 1-12; Table 2 visually checked on PDF page 7. No appendices in this version.

## Research question

Users may omit database identities and precise constraints while requesting information spanning heterogeneous data sources.

## Method

TACO combines a restricted expert-curated smart-city set with synthetic open-data queries. TACO-SQL rewrites questions, retrieves tables with a trained dual encoder, and plans SQL-only execution pipelines with error repair.

## Evaluation

Execution accuracy is reported across real/synthetic subsets. The TL ablation supplies gold relevant tables, whereas QR+TL performs retrieval after rewriting. A 240-example human sample evaluates synthetic quality. Public and controlled-access subsets must be distinguished.

## What the results support

Retrieval and planning improve several tested models, though gains vary by model/configuration. Larger schemas and cross-database queries remain difficult. These are single-turn reference-result scores, not measurement of all interpretations or user clarification success.

## Limits and qualifications

Rewriting infers an intended reading without user confirmation. Synthetic examples remain reference-conditioned; the quality-control prose and table report inconsistent scores. SmartCity access requires a data-use agreement or author-run evaluation, and the released public snapshot differs from the paper's total.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

Useful for studying table discovery and cross-database planning under underspecified requests, with explicit protocol and access boundaries.

## Checks against the paper

These are interpretations checked against the source, not verbatim quotations attributed to its authors.
